paper_title: Can LLMs Solve longer Math Word Problems Better
caption: (left) and (right) of scaling up SFT dataset across various model scales in the LLaMA-2 family. The results suggest scaling up model scales and SFT dataset can further improve .
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the performance of three LLaMA-2 model variants — LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-2-13B, and LLaMA-2-70B — on the CoLeG-R benchmark (%), under four different supervised fine-tuning (SFT) conditions: no SFT (light blue with diagonal stripes), + SFT on D₀ (orange with horizontal stripes), + SFT on D₀, D₁ (light purple with diagonal stripes), and + SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂ (solid pink). The vertical axis represents CoLeG-R score in percentage, ranging from 0 to 85 with major ticks every 10 units. For each model size, the bars are grouped side-by-side in the order of increasing SFT dataset scope. Performance consistently improves with both larger model scale and broader SFT dataset: for example, LLaMA-2-7B scores ~67% with no SFT and ~83% with full SFT (D₀–D₂); LLaMA-2-13B improves from ~70% to ~80%; and LLaMA-2-70B rises from ~80% to ~83%. The chart visually supports the claim that scaling both model size and SFT dataset leads to better performance on longer math word problems, as reflected in higher CoLeG-R scores.
